text:
Alex: Heads-up — discovered a copy/paste mismatch in the quickstart README. JS snippet expects REDWOOD_API_KEY but the Python snippet uses REDWOOD_KEY. New users are getting confused during signup flow.

Priya: Oh no, that's annoying. I ran into a support ticket earlier where someone pasted REDWOOD_TOKEN and it failed.

Sam: Yikes. Can you paste the snippets? I can open a tiny PR.

Alex: Here are the problematic bits: 
```javascript
// js snippet in README
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
```
```python
# python snippet in README
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_KEY"))
```

Priya: We should standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere and add a note that the SDKs will also check REDWOOD_TOKEN and ~/.redwood/credentials for backwards compat. That'll reduce support noise.

Jules: Agree. Also suggest adding a tiny snippet smoke-test in CI that runs both snippets (or at least parses them) so docs drift gets caught. We've had multiple auth var mismatches before.

Sam: I'll open PR to replace REDWOOD_KEY with REDWOOD_API_KEY, add a short paragraph about credential precedence, and add a link to the env var reference in the console.

Alex: Awesome, thanks @Sam. Can you also add a one-line callout for token rotation so people don't store tokens in code?

Sam: Yup. Will target a 1-line change + CI doc lint job. Drafting now.

DocsBot: docs-lint failed on main for sample-snippets.md in last run (see CI run #4821) — looks related to snippet formatting.

Priya: Perfect timing — Sam, if you need me to sanity-check the wording for the credential precedence note I can review.

Sam: Will ping you in the PR, thanks.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Small change but big DX impact :thumbsup:
